title: Debug lifetime bug in Rust — 3 turns
description: Function returns a reference to a local String (doesn't compile). Fix by returning owned value, run tests, refactor to use Arc for shared ownership.

task_spec.prompt: The `make_greeting` function in `src/lib.rs` returns an empty `String::new()` instead of the formatted greeting. Fix it to return `format!("Hello, {}!", name)`. Run `cargo test --quiet`.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test --quiet` to check the current state. Walk me through what you fixed. Look at `GreetingCache` — it uses `Arc<String>` correctly already, but make sure `store()` and `get()` compile and work. If any tests are failing, fix them.

Final step: refactor `make_greeting` to use `Arc<String>` if you haven't already — actually keep it returning `String` (that's correct), but add a new method `GreetingCache::store_greeting(name: &str)` that calls make_greeting internally and stores the result. Add a test if you can. Then run `cargo test --quiet` — all 5 existing tests must pass.
success_criteria: make_greeting returns correctly formatted greeting string
get() returns None when cache is empty
